subject.title: fix: harden Mattermost slash callback auth

question: Should OpenClaw fail closed on any non-HTTPS Mattermost native slash callback URL before registration, even for existing HTTP callback deployments?
rationale: The code change is small and appears correctly placed, but it deliberately breaks current HTTP callback deployments while changing a token-bearing callback boundary, so maintainer/security intent is required.

options.title: Require HTTPS fail-closed after proof
options.body: Accept the security hardening once the contributor supplies redacted live Mattermost proof, refreshes the conflicted branch/body, and maintainers approve the upgrade break.

options.title: Stage compatibility instead
options.body: Ask for a staged migration, doctor guidance, or opt-in strict mode if existing HTTP callback deployments must continue by default.

options.title: Decline the transport break
options.body: Keep the current warn-and-register behavior if maintainers decide cleartext callback deployments remain supported despite the token exposure risk.

recommendation.title: Require HTTPS fail-closed after proof
recommendation.body: Accept the security hardening once the contributor supplies redacted live Mattermost proof, refreshes the conflicted branch/body, and maintainers approve the upgrade break.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest current-main ownership around monitor slash registration and adjacent callback/token hardening.
